objects.summary: P1 review rejects the rule requiring two READY tasks at all times: when all positive-value work is complete or blocked, legitimate IDLE must be allowed to avoid invented work and low-information experiments.
P2 review finds team-status/watchdog parsers recognize only Q* task rows while permanent B/C/D lanes can contain READY/open work; this can falsely report no work and suppress silence alerts.

P2 review finds required fetches include branches cited only by DONE tasks; normal deletion of a completed-task branch can therefore abort current coordination. Only active branches should be mandatory, while DONE branch absence is non-blocking.
P2 review closes another checksum loophole: every explicitly declared SHA must have its own matching block; a digest merely appearing inside another verified block cannot satisfy the declaration.

cross_object_findings.finding: A continuous-work rule without a legitimate IDLE state creates artificial tasks and consumes budget after useful work is exhausted or blocked. Continuity must mean next useful action, not perpetual activity.
Hardcoded Q-prefix assumptions became stale as B/C/D lanes were introduced, allowing real open work to disappear from coordination logic.
Historical branch lifecycle must not make current coordination fail closed after task completion; durable commit identity is enough for completed work while active branches remain strict.
Publication verification must require one exact block for every declared digest; cross-reference text cannot satisfy a missing publication object.
